reviews.body:
Ran the Mistral ITs with a real key: all green (`MistralAiModelsSmokeIT` with all 7 models, `MistralAiHttpClientTimeoutIT`, `BlankTurnRePromptIT`).

I also checked the request body sent to `ministral-8b-2512`:
- penalties set: `"presence_penalty":0.5,"frequency_penalty":0.3` is sent, and the call works.
- penalties not set: `0.0` is sent for both, same as on main and Mistral's default.

Also ran every model with and without penalties: 14/14 OK.

@pcbeingused333  Good job!

comments.body:
@pcbeingused333 - please elaborate on how the issue was discovered.
Please confirm successful execution of IT tests, thanks

Discovery: found by reading the code, not from a runtime failure. `MistralAiOptionsConverter` builds `MistralAiChatOptions` from model, temperature, topP and maxTokens only, while the OpenAI converters in this repo also forward `presencePenalty`/`frequencyPenalty`, and `MistralAiChatOptions` supports both. This is the same class as #2218 (Ollama dropping `maxTokens`). The unit test `MistralAiOptionsConverterTest` shows the penalties come back as the default `0.0` on main and pass through with the change.

IT tests: I have not run the Mistral ITs. They need a real `MISTRAL_API_KEY` and none is available here, so I can't confirm they pass. The change is limited to the converter and covered by the unit test. If you can run the ITs on your side, or want me to drop the PR, say so.

(Prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent.)

@pcbeingused333 - please confirm whether the code in fact was analyzed by AI assistant as well. If yes, please share a prompt.
I replied separately with guidance and expectations for contributors.

Thanks for understanding.
looping @azanux

@igordayen yes, the code was analyzed with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). It compared the option converters across providers and flagged that the Mistral one drops `presencePenalty`/`frequencyPenalty`, which the OpenAI converters forward. The patch and the unit test came out of that session. I'd rather not paste the prompt itself; it was a general instruction to look for request options that a provider converter silently drops, with no instructions specific to Embabel.

I'll read your contributor guidance. On the ITs: I'll run the Mistral ITs once I have a key and post the actual output here. Until then, the only coverage is the unit test.

@pcbeingused333 - thanks, Alex.
PR will then be open till  IT tests successful completion.
